newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower despite crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower despite crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to down slightly late Tuesday in quiet trade, with soft gas prices and mild weather forecasts offsetting a modest NYMEX crude rally, industry sources said.

"(Firmer) crude today kept things in check, but there's beem some downward pressure. There's still a lot of overhang in the market," said one cash trader, noting talk of more barrels from Venezuela pressured high sulphurs again today.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held relatively steady at $16.25-50 a barrel, with March one percent paper also talked little changed at about $16, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour also notionally were flat at $19.25 and $17.25-50, respectively.
NYH high sulphurs again were down slightly, with 2.2 percent now at $15.00-25.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent slipped a quarter to $14.75-15.00.
Traders said USG three percent was 25-50 cents lower at $12.75 after reports late Monday of a small, prompt sale at $12.50 (FOB Miss. River).

New York city gate February and March gas prices were talked Tuesday at about the $2.10/mmBtu level, or about $13.23 a barrel equivalent. Feb gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell by almost 10 cents to the low-$1.80s/mmBtu, or $11.53 a barrel equivalent.
